stem: Manganese, $\text{Mn}$, and its compounds are widely used in many chemical reactions.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem: $\text{Mn}$ is usually found as a single isotope, manganese-55.
parts.text: Determine the number of protons, neutrons and electrons in an atom of manganese-55.

parts.label: (a)(iii)
parts.text:
A sample of manganese from the Moon is found to contain manganese-53 in addition to manganese-55.

State the two pieces of information needed to determine the relative atomic mass, $A_{\text{r}}$, of manganese in this sample.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: The shorthand electronic configuration of manganese is $[\text{Ar}] 3\text{d}^5 4\text{s}^2$.
parts.text: Complete the full electronic configuration of manganese.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Deduce the total number of unpaired electrons in an atom of manganese.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
Manganese(IV) oxide reacts with methanal, $\text{CH}_2\text{O}$, in acidic conditions to produce carbon dioxide. The movement of electrons to or from relevant species is shown in the following half-equations.

half-equation 1 $$\text{CH}_2\text{O} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + 4\text{H}^+ + 4\text{e}^-$$

half-equation 2 $$\text{MnO}_2 + 4\text{H}^+ + 2\text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$$
parts.text: Identify the species that is reduced in half-equation 2. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
The oxidation state of carbon in methanal is 0.

Calculate the oxidation state of carbon in carbon dioxide.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Construct the ionic equation for the reaction of manganese(IV) oxide with methanal in acidic conditions.
